# Data Visualization Skill

Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.

## Chart Selection Guide

### Choose by Data Relationship

| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |

### When NOT to Use Certain Charts

- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.

## Python Visualization Code Patterns

### Setup and Style

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Professional style setup
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# Colorblind-friendly palettes
PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']
PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'
PALETTE_DIVERGING = 'RdBu_r'
```

### Line Chart (Time Series)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for label, group in df.groupby('category'):
    ax.plot(group['date'], group['value'], label=label, linewidth=2)

ax.set_title('Metric Trend by Category', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Date')
ax.set_ylabel('Value')
ax.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Format dates on x-axis
fig.autofmt_xdate()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('trend_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Bar Chart (Comparison)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Sort by value for easy reading
df_sorted = df.sort_values('metric', ascending=True)

bars = ax.barh(df_sorted['category'], df_sorted['metric'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0])

# Add value labels
for bar in bars:
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax.text(width + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{width:,.0f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=10)

ax.set_title('Metric by Category (Ranked)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Metric Value')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('bar_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Histogram (Distribution)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

ax.hist(df['value'], bins=30, color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0], edgecolor='white', alpha=0.8)

# Add mean and median lines
mean_val = df['value'].mean()
median_val = df['value'].median()
ax.axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Mean: {mean_val:,.1f}')
ax.axvline(median_val, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Median: {median_val:,.1f}')

ax.set_title('Distribution of Values', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Value')
ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax.legend()
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

### brief
# Renewable Energy Cost Revolution: LCOE, Capacity & Fossil Fuel Subsidies (2010–2024)

## Overview
This collection of four datasets tracks the economic transformation of the global energy sector from 2010 to 2024. It covers the declining levelized cost of energy for solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage; the cost range of new fossil fuel generation; cumulative renewable installed capacity; and annual global fossil fuel subsidies.

## Data Source

### lcoe_trends
Annual LCOE values for three technologies: `solar_pv`, `onshore_wind`, and `battery_storage`. All values in 2023 real USD per MWh. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV ranges from 359 to 33; onshore wind from 95 to 35; battery storage from 1,100 to 102.

### fossil_fuel_lcoe_range
Biennial LCOE ranges for new-build gas CCGT (`gas_ccgt_low`, `gas_ccgt_high`) and coal (`coal_low`, `coal_high`). 8 rows at even-year intervals. Values in 2023 real USD/MWh. These define the reference band against which renewable crossover points are identified.

### installed_capacity
Cumulative global installed capacity in GW for `solar_pv_gw` and `onshore_wind_gw`. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV grows from 40 to 1,950 GW; onshore wind from 178 to 960 GW.

### fossil_fuel_subsidies
Annual global fossil fuel subsidies in nominal billion USD, split into `consumption_subsidies_bn` and `production_subsidies_bn`, with a `total_subsidies_bn` sum. 15 rows (2010–2024). Total ranges from ~290 to ~700 billion.

## Data Notes
- LCOE figures are illustrative estimates aligned with IRENA and BloombergNEF reporting trends but rounded for clarity.

with DATA_PATH.open() as f:
    source = json.load(f)

lcoe = pd.DataFrame(source['lcoe_trends']['data'])
fossil = pd.DataFrame(source['fossil_fuel_lcoe_range']['data'])
capacity = pd.DataFrame(source['installed_capacity']['data'])
subsidies = pd.DataFrame(source['fossil_fuel_subsidies']['data'])

years = lcoe['year'].to_numpy()
fossil_annual = fossil.set_index('year').reindex(years).interpolate(method='index').reset_index()
fossil_annual['range_low'] = fossil_annual[['gas_ccgt_low', 'coal_low']].min(axis=1)
fossil_annual['range_high'] = fossil_annual[['gas_ccgt_high', 'coal_high']].max(axis=1)

# First year each technology falls below the lower edge of the interpolated fossil new-build range.
crossovers = {}
for tech in ['solar_pv', 'onshore_wind']:
    below = lcoe[tech].to_numpy() < fossil_annual['range_low'].to_numpy()
    crossovers[tech] = int(years[np.argmax(below)]) if below.any() else None

plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.dpi': 180,
    'savefig.dpi': 240,
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'font.size': 10.5,
    'axes.titlesize': 12,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 10,
    'xtick.labelsize': 9,
    'ytick.labelsize': 9,
    'legend.fontsize': 8.8,
    'axes.edgecolor': '#D0D6DC',
    'grid.color': '#E8EDF2',
    'grid.linewidth': 0.75,
})

colors = {
    'solar': '#F2A900',
    'wind': '#2C7FB8',
    'battery': '#6A51A3',

    'capacity_solar': '#E6A100',
    'capacity_wind': '#1F78B4',
}

fig = plt.figure(figsize=(14.2, 9.4), facecolor='white')
gs = GridSpec(2, 2, figure=fig, width_ratios=[1.28, 1], height_ratios=[1, 0.82], hspace=0.34, wspace=0.22)
ax_lcoe = fig.add_subplot(gs[:, 0])
ax_capacity = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
ax_subsidy = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])

# Main LCOE panel with log scale to show battery collapse while preserving solar/wind crossover detail.
ax_lcoe.fill_between(
    fossil_annual['year'].to_numpy(),
    fossil_annual['range_low'].to_numpy(),
    fossil_annual['range_high'].to_numpy(),
    color=colors['fossil'], alpha=0.18, linewidth=0, label='New fossil generation range'
)
ax_lcoe.plot(fossil_annual['year'], fossil_annual['range_low'], color=colors['fossil'], lw=1.0, alpha=0.5)
ax_lcoe.plot(fossil_annual['year'], fossil_annual['range_high'], color=colors['fossil'], lw=1.0, alpha=0.5)

series = [
    ('solar_pv', 'Solar PV', colors['solar'], 'o'),
    ('onshore_wind', 'Onshore wind', colors['wind'], 's'),
    ('battery_storage', 'Battery storage (4h)', colors['battery'], '^'),
]
for field, label, color, marker in series:
    ax_lcoe.plot(lcoe['year'], lcoe[field], lw=3, color=color, marker=marker, ms=5.2, label=label)

ax_lcoe.set_yscale('log')
ax_lcoe.set_ylim(25, 1350)
ax_lcoe.set_xlim(2009.6, 2024.6)
ax_lcoe.set_title('Renewable costs collapsed below fossil new-build economics', loc='left', pad=12)
ax_lcoe.set_xlabel('Year')
ax_lcoe.set_ylabel('Levelized cost of energy, USD/MWh (2023 real dollars, log scale)')
ax_lcoe.yaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.FixedLocator([25, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000]))
ax_lcoe.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f'${x:,.0f}'))
ax_lcoe.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(2))
ax_lcoe.xaxis.set_minor_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(1))

# Crossover annotations.
for tech, label, color, yoff in [
    ('solar_pv', 'Solar below fossil range', colors['solar'], 1.28),
    ('onshore_wind', 'Wind below fossil range', colors['wind'], 0.78),
]:
    year = crossovers[tech]
    value = float(lcoe.loc[lcoe['year'] == year, tech].iloc[0])
    ax_lcoe.scatter([year], [value], s=145, color=color, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1.8, zorder=5)
    ax_lcoe.axvline(year, ymin=0.04, ymax=0.94, color=color, lw=1.4, ls=(0, (3, 4)), alpha=0.68)
    ax_lcoe.annotate(
        f'{year}: {label}\n${value:.0f}/MWh',
        xy=(year, value),
        xytext=(year - 4.1, value * yoff),
        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-|>', color=color, lw=1.3, shrinkA=4, shrinkB=6, connectionstyle='arc3,rad=0.16'),
        color='#1F2937', fontsize=9.2, fontweight='bold',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.35', fc='white', ec=color, lw=1.0, alpha=0.95)
    )

# Endpoint labels and percentage declines.
declines = {
    'solar_pv': (1 - lcoe['solar_pv'].iloc[-1] / lcoe['solar_pv'].iloc[0]) * 100,
    'onshore_wind': (1 - lcoe['onshore_wind'].iloc[-1] / lcoe['onshore_wind'].iloc[0]) * 100,
    'battery_storage': (1 - lcoe['battery_storage'].iloc[-1] / lcoe['battery_storage'].iloc[0]) * 100,
}
end_labels = [
    ('solar_pv', 'Solar PV', colors['solar'], 1.02),
    ('onshore_wind', 'Wind', colors['wind'], 0.90),
    ('battery_storage', 'Battery', colors['battery'], 1.03),
]
for field, label, color, mult in end_labels:
    y = lcoe[field].iloc[-1]
    ax_lcoe.text(2024.23, y * mult, f'{label}: ${y:.0f}\n−{declines[field]:.0f}%', color=color,
                 fontsize=9.4, fontweight='bold', va='center')

ax_lcoe.text(2010.1, 1180, 'Battery storage fell\nfrom $1,100 to $102/MWh', color=colors['battery'],
             fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', va='top')
ax_lcoe.text(2010.1, 39, 'Gray band: min–max LCOE range\nfor new gas CCGT and coal', color='#4B5563', fontsize=8.8)

handles_lcoe = [
    Patch(facecolor=colors['fossil'], alpha=0.18, label='New fossil generation range'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors['solar'], marker='o', lw=3, label='Solar PV'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors['wind'], marker='s', lw=3, label='Onshore wind'),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors['battery'], marker='^', lw=3, label='Battery storage'),
]
ax_lcoe.legend(handles=handles_lcoe, loc='upper right', frameon=True, framealpha=0.96, title='Cost series')

# Capacity panel.
ax_capacity.plot(capacity['year'], capacity['solar_pv_gw'], color=colors['capacity_solar'], lw=3.1, marker='o', ms=4.7, label='Solar PV capacity')
ax_capacity.plot(capacity['year'], capacity['onshore_wind_gw'], color=colors['capacity_wind'], lw=3.1, marker='s', ms=4.7, label='Onshore wind capacity')
ax_capacity.fill_between(capacity['year'].to_numpy(), capacity['solar_pv_gw'].to_numpy(), color=colors['capacity_solar'], alpha=0.13)
ax_capacity.fill_between(capacity['year'].to_numpy(), capacity['onshore_wind_gw'].to_numpy(), color=colors['capacity_wind'], alpha=0.10)
ax_capacity.axvspan(2018, 2024, color=colors['capacity_solar'], alpha=0.08, lw=0)
ax_capacity.annotate('Solar acceleration\nafter 2018', xy=(2022.6, 1185), xytext=(2018.55, 1570),
                     arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-|>', color=colors['capacity_solar'], lw=1.2, connectionstyle='arc3,rad=-0.16'),
                     fontsize=9.2, fontweight='bold', color='#7A4F00',
                     bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.3', fc='white', ec='#F0C55C', alpha=0.94))
ax_capacity.text(2024.15, capacity['solar_pv_gw'].iloc[-1], '1,950 GW', color=colors['capacity_solar'], fontweight='bold', va='center')
ax_capacity.text(2024.15, capacity['onshore_wind_gw'].iloc[-1], '960 GW', color=colors['capacity_wind'], fontweight='bold', va='center')
ax_capacity.set_title('Deployment scaled as costs fell', loc='left', pad=10)
ax_capacity.set_ylabel('Cumulative installed capacity (GW)')
ax_capacity.set_xlabel('Year')
ax_capacity.set_xlim(2009.7, 2025.0)
ax_capacity.set_ylim(0, 2150)
ax_capacity.xaxis.set_major_locator(mticker.MultipleLocator(2))
ax_capacity.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f'{x:,.0f}'))
ax_capacity.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, framealpha=0.95)
